cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's Tax Machine prepare Forms 1099-NEC, the yearly report of contractor pay, for HANGS Construction Services.
Next, every payment made to vendors this year, checked against the accounts payable ledger.
In all, about $2.3 million went to 18 vendors.
Now it checks the official rules online, including this year's higher reporting threshold.
Each rule is matched to the client's records.
Then it sorts every payment. Corporations, materials and card charges are left out.
Nine contractors get a form, for about $708,000 in all.
One vendor never gave a tax ID, so tax should have been withheld from its payments.
Every payment ties back to the year's total.
Last, it writes the draft forms and the workpapers behind them.

All done. Nine draft forms report $708,088 paid to contractors. Five items stay open, including a tax ID that doesn't match IRS records, $1,344 of withholding never taken, and a worker who may be an employee. A person reviews and e-files by February 1; nothing is filed yet.
Here are the results: nine draft forms reporting $708,088, and five open items for a person to decide.
